fields.api: Enable the control API server, which allows to control the server.
fields.apiServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is yes.
fields.apiTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the HTTP server. These proxies can use the X-Forwarded-For header to set the real IP of clients, and the X-Forwarded-Proto header to set the original protocol.
fields.dumpPackets: Dump packets to disk. This is useful for debugging.
fields.logDestinations: Destinations of log messages; available values are stdout, file and syslog.
fields.logFile: When file is in logDestinations, this is the file which will receive logs.
fields.logLevel: Verbosity of the program; available values are error, warn, info, debug.
fields.logStructured: When destination is stdout or file, emit logs in structured format (JSONL).
fields.sysLogPrefix: When syslog is in logDestinations, use prefix for logs.
fields.udpMaxPayloadSize: Maximum size of outgoing UDP payloads. It defaults to the maximum packet size on ethernet (1500) minus IPv6 and UDP headers (48). This can be decreased to avoid fragmentation on networks with a low MTU.
fields.udpReadBufferSize: Size of the read buffer of every UDP socket. This can be increased to decrease packet losses. It defaults to the default value of the operating system.
fields.writeQueueSize: Size of the queue of outgoing packets. A higher value allows to increase throughput, a lower value allows to save RAM.
fields.authMethod: Authentication method. Available values: internal — credentials are stored in the configuration file; http — an external HTTP URL is contacted for each authentication request; jwt — credentials are signed tokens released by an external identity server.
fields.authHTTPAddress: URL called to perform authentication. Every time a user wants to perform an action, the server calls this URL with the POST method and a payload described in the documentation. If the response code is 20x, the action is allowed, otherwise it is forbidden.
fields.authHTTPExclude: Actions to exclude from HTTP-based authentication. Format is the same as the one of user permissions.
fields.authHTTPFingerprint: If the HTTP authentication URL has a self-signed or invalid certificate, you can provide the fingerprint of the certificate in order to validate it anyway.
fields.authJWTAudience: Expected audience (aud) claim in the JWT. Leave empty to skip validation.
fields.authJWTClaimKey: Name of the claim that contains permissions.
fields.authJWTExclude: Actions to exclude from JWT-based authentication. Format is the same as the one of user permissions.
fields.authJWTIssuer: Expected issuer (iss) claim in the JWT. Leave empty to skip validation.
fields.authJWTJWKS: This is the JWKS URL that will be used to pull (once) the public key that allows to validate JWTs.
fields.authJWTJWKSFingerprint: If the JWKS URL has a self-signed or invalid certificate, you can provide the fingerprint of the certificate in order to validate it anyway.
fields.metrics: Enable the metrics server, which allows to extract Prometheus-compatible metrics.
fields.metricsServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is yes.
fields.metricsTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the HTTP server. These proxies can use the X-Forwarded-For header to set the real IP of clients, and the X-Forwarded-Proto header to set the original protocol.
fields.pprof: Enable the PPROF server, which allows to extract performance reports.
fields.pprofServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is yes.
fields.pprofTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the HTTP server. These proxies can use the X-Forwarded-For header to set the real IP of clients, and the X-Forwarded-Proto header to set the original protocol.
fields.playback: Enable the playback server, which allows to download recordings from the server.
fields.playbackServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is yes.
fields.playbackTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the HTTP server. These proxies can use the X-Forwarded-For header to set the real IP of clients, and the X-Forwarded-Proto header to set the original protocol.
fields.hls: Enable the HLS server, which allows to read streams with the HLS protocol.
fields.hlsAlwaysRemux: By default, HLS is generated only when requested by a user. This option allows to generate it always, avoiding the delay between request and generation.
fields.hlsCDNSecret: Secret to identify requests coming from a CDN. The CDN must insert this secret in every request in the Authorization: Bearer header.
fields.hlsDirectory: Directory in which to save segments and non-low-latency playlists. This has two purposes: offloading RAM and creating a self-consistent directory that can be served by a CDN.
fields.hlsEncryption: Enable HTTPS. This is required for Low-Latency HLS to function correctly on Apple devices.
fields.hlsMuxerCloseAfter: The muxer will be closed when there are no reader requests and this amount of time has passed.
fields.hlsPartDuration: Minimum duration of each part. A player usually puts 3 parts in a buffer before reproducing the stream. Parts are used in Low-Latency HLS in place of segments. Part duration is influenced by the distance between video/audio samples and is adjusted in order to produce segments with a similar duration.
fields.hlsSegmentCount: Number of HLS segments to keep on the server. Segments allow to seek through the stream. Their number doesn't influence latency.
fields.hlsSegmentDuration: Minimum duration of each segment. A player usually puts 3 segments in a buffer before reproducing the stream. The final segment duration is also influenced by the interval between IDR frames, since the server changes the duration in order to include at least one IDR frame in each segment.
fields.hlsSegmentMaxSize: Maximum size of each segment. This prevents RAM exhaustion.
fields.hlsServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is yes.
fields.hlsTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the HLS server. If the server receives a request from one of these entries, IP in logs will be taken from the X-Forwarded-For header.
fields.hlsVariant: Variant of the HLS protocol to use. Available options are: mpegts — uses MPEG-TS segments, for maximum compatibility; fmp4 — uses fragmented MP4 segments, more efficient; lowLatency — uses Low-Latency HLS.
fields.moq: Enable the MoQ (Media over QUIC) server, which allows to publish and read streams with the MoQ protocol.
fields.moqHTTP2Address: Address of the TCP/HTTP2 listener. This hosts the web client.
fields.moqHTTP3Address: Address of the UDP/HTTP3 listener. This hosts the WebTransport endpoint.
fields.moqQUICAddress: Address of the UDP/QUIC listener used for native MoQ-over-QUIC.
fields.moqServerKey: Path to the server key. If set to auto.key, a key is generated automatically and saved in the current folder.
fields.moqTrustedProxies: Proxies which are trusted to provide the client's real IP via the X-Forwarded-For header.
fields.rtmp: Enable the RTMP server, which allows to publish and read streams with the RTMP protocol.
fields.rtmpAddress: Address of the TCP/RTMP listener. This is needed only when encryption is no or optional.
fields.rtmpEncryption: Use the secure protocol variant (RTMPS). Available values are no, strict, optional.
fields.rtmpServerCert: Path to the server certificate. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtmpServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtmpTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the RTMP server. If the server receives a request from one of these entries, IP in logs and authentication will be taken from the PROXY protocol header.
fields.rtmpsAddress: Address of the TCP/RTMPS listener. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtsp: Enable the RTSP server, which allows to publish and read streams with the RTSP protocol.
fields.rtspAddress: Address of the TCP/RTSP listener. This is needed only when encryption is no or optional.
fields.rtspAuthMethods: Authentication methods. Available are basic and digest. digest doesn't provide any additional security and is available for compatibility only.
fields.rtspEncryption: Use secure protocol variants (RTSPS, SRTP, SRTCP). Available values are no, strict, optional.
fields.rtspServerCert: Path to the server certificate. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtspServerKey: Path to the server key. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtspTransports: Enabled RTSP transport protocols. The handshake is always performed with TCP.
fields.rtspTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the RTSP server. If the server receives a request from one of these entries, IP in logs and authentication will be taken from the PROXY protocol header.
fields.rtspsAddress: Address of the TCP/RTSPS listener. This is needed only when encryption is strict or optional.
fields.rtpAddress: Address of the UDP/RTP listener. This is needed only when udp is in rtspTransports and encryption is no or optional.
fields.rtcpAddress: Address of the UDP/RTCP listener. This is needed only when udp is in rtspTransports and encryption is no or optional.
fields.srtpAddress: Address of the UDP/SRTP listener. This is needed only when udp is in rtspTransports and encryption is strict or optional.
fields.srtcpAddress: Address of the UDP/SRTCP listener. This is needed only when udp is in rtspTransports and encryption is strict or optional.
fields.srt: Enable the SRT server, which allows to publish and read streams with the SRT protocol.
fields.webrtc: Enable the WebRTC server, which allows to publish and read streams with the WebRTC protocol.
fields.webrtcAdditionalHosts: Additional hosts or IPs to send to clients.
fields.webrtcAddress: Address of the WebRTC TCP/HTTP listener.
fields.webrtcEncryption: Enable HTTPS. This covers only the WebRTC handshake, while WebRTC streams are always encrypted with a key that is exchanged during the WebRTC handshake.
fields.webrtcHandshakeTimeout: Time to wait for the WebRTC handshake to complete.
fields.webrtcICEServers2: ICE servers. Needed only when local listeners can't be reached by clients. STUN servers allow to obtain and share the public IP of the server. TURN/TURNS servers force all traffic through them.
fields.webrtcIPsFromInterfaces: WebRTC clients need to know the IP of the server. Gather IPs from interfaces and send them to clients.
fields.webrtcIPsFromInterfacesExcludeList: Interfaces whose IPs will NOT be sent to clients. This is useful to exclude specific interfaces (e.g. VPN tunnels) while using all others.
fields.webrtcIPsFromInterfacesList: Interfaces whose IPs will be sent to clients. An empty value means to use all available interfaces.
fields.webrtcLocalTCPAddress: Address of a TCP/ICE listener that will receive connections. This is disabled by default since TCP is less efficient than UDP and introduces a progressive delay when network is congested.
fields.webrtcLocalUDPAddress: Address of a UDP/ICE listener that will receive connections. Use a blank string to disable.
fields.webrtcSTUNGatherTimeout: Maximum time to gather STUN candidates.
fields.webrtcTrustedProxies: IPs or CIDRs of proxies placed before the WebRTC server. If the server receives a request from one of these entries, IP in logs will be taken from the X-Forwarded-For header.
fields.multicastIPRange: IP range of all UDP-multicast listeners. This is needed only when multicast is in rtspTransports and encryption is no or optional.
fields.multicastRTCPPort: Port of all UDP-multicast/RTCP listeners. This is needed only when multicast is in rtspTransports and encryption is no or optional.
fields.multicastRTPPort: Port of all UDP-multicast/RTP listeners. This is needed only when multicast is in rtspTransports and encryption is no or optional.
fields.multicastSRTCPPort: Port of all UDP-multicast/SRTCP listeners. This is needed only when multicast is in rtspTransports and encryption is strict or optional.
fields.multicastSRTPPort: Port of all UDP-multicast/SRTP listeners. This is needed only when multicast is in rtspTransports and encryption is strict or optional.
fields.runOnConnect: Command to run when a client connects to the server. This is terminated with SIGINT when a client disconnects from the server.
fields.runOnConnectRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnDisconnect: Command to run when a client disconnects from the server.
fields.source: Source of the stream. Can be publisher (stream provided by an RTSP/RTMP/WebRTC/SRT client) or a pull URL: rtsp://, rtsps://, rtsp+http://, rtsps+http://, rtsp+ws://, rtsps+ws://, rtmp://…#streamKey, rtmps://…#streamKey, http(s)://…/stream.m3u8, udp+mpegts://ip:port, unix+mpegts://socketPath, udp+rtp://ip:port, srt://host:port?streamid=…, moqt://…, whep(s)://host:port/path, redirect, or rpiCamera. Variables: $MTX_QUERY (query params, passed by first reader), $G1, $G2, … (regex groups if path name is a regex).
fields.sourceFingerprint: If the source is a URL, and the source TLS certificate is self-signed or invalid, you can provide the fingerprint of the certificate in order to validate it anyway.
fields.sourceOnDemand: If the source is a URL, it will be pulled only when at least one reader is connected, saving bandwidth.
fields.sourceOnDemandStartTimeout: If sourceOnDemand is yes, readers will be put on hold until the source is ready or until this amount of time has passed.
fields.sourceOnDemandCloseAfter: If sourceOnDemand is yes, the source will be closed when there are no readers connected and this amount of time has passed.
fields.sourceRedirect: Path to which clients will be redirected. It can be a relative path (i.e. /otherstream) or an absolute RTSP URL.
fields.maxReaders: Maximum number of readers. Zero means no limit.
fields.useAbsoluteTimestamp: Use absolute timestamp of frames, instead of replacing them with the current time.
fields.alwaysAvailable: Enable always-available mode, in which an offline segment is played on repeat when the stream is not available.
fields.alwaysAvailableFile: An MP4 file can be used instead of the default offline segment.
fields.alwaysAvailableRecorded: If recording is enabled, record the stream even while the source is offline and the offline segment is playing. Set to false to record only while a source is connected.
fields.alwaysAvailableTracks: Tracks of the default offline segment.
fields.recordDeleteAfter: Delete segments after this timespan. Set to 0s to disable automatic deletion.
fields.recordFormat: Format of recorded segments. Available formats are fmp4 (fragmented MP4) and mpegts (MPEG-TS).
fields.recordPartDuration: fMP4 segments are concatenation of small MP4 files (parts), each with this duration. MPEG-TS segments are concatenation of 188-bytes packets, flushed to disk with this period. When a system failure occurs, the last part gets lost. Therefore, the part duration is equal to the RPO (recovery point objective).
fields.recordPath: Path of recording segments. Extension is added automatically. Available variables are %path (path name), %Y %m %d (year, month, day), %H %M %S (hours, minutes, seconds), %f (microseconds), %z (time zone), %s (unix epoch).
fields.overridePublisher: Allow another client to disconnect the current publisher and publish in its place.
fields.srtPublishPassphrase: SRT encryption passphrase required to publish to this path.
fields.srtReadPassphrase: SRT encryption passphrase required to read from this path.
fields.rtspDemuxMpegts: Demux MPEG-TS over RTSP into elementary streams. When enabled, RTSP publishers and sources sending a single MP2T/90000 track will be demultiplexed, and their elementary streams (H.264, H.265, AAC, etc.) exposed as native tracks. This allows HLS, WebRTC, and other outputs to work transparently with MPEG-TS sources.
fields.rtspTransport: Transport protocol used to pull the stream. Available values are automatic, udp, multicast, tcp.
fields.rtspAnyPort: Support sources that don't provide server ports or use random server ports. This is a security issue and must be used only when interacting with sources that require it.
fields.rtspRangeType: Range header to send to the source, in order to start streaming from the specified offset. Available values: clock — absolute time; npt — Normal Play Time; smpte — SMPTE timestamps relative to the start of the recording.
fields.rtspRangeStart: Available values: clock — UTC ISO 8601 combined date and time string, e.g. 20230812T120000Z; npt — duration such as 300ms, 1.5m or 2h45m (units: ns, us, ms, s, m, h); smpte — duration such as 300ms, 1.5m or 2h45m (units: ns, us, ms, s, m, h).
fields.rtspScale: Scale header value to send to the source, in order to play the stream at a different speed. Negative values play in reverse, values > 1 fast-forward, values 0 < x < 1 play slow motion.
fields.rtspUDPSourcePortRange: Range of ports used as source port in outgoing UDP packets.
fields.rtpSDP: Session Description Protocol (SDP) of the RTP stream.
fields.moqTransport: Transport protocol used to pull the stream. Available values are quic, webtransport.
fields.whepBearerToken: Token to insert in the Authorization: Bearer header.
fields.whepSTUNGatherTimeout: Maximum time to gather STUN candidates.
fields.whepHandshakeTimeout: Time to wait for the WebRTC handshake to complete.
fields.rpiCameraSecondary: Whether this is a secondary stream.
fields.rpiCameraExposure: Exposure mode. Values: normal, short, long, custom.
fields.rpiCameraAWB: Auto-white-balance mode. (auto, incandescent, tungsten, fluorescent, indoor, daylight, cloudy or custom).
fields.rpiCameraAWBGains: Auto-white-balance fixed gains. This can be used in place of rpiCameraAWB. Format: [red, blue].
fields.rpiCameraDenoise: Denoise operating mode (off, cdn_off, cdn_fast, cdn_hq).
fields.rpiCameraMetering: Metering mode of the AEC/AGC algorithm (centre, spot, matrix or custom).
fields.rpiCameraEV: EV compensation of the image in range [-10, 10].
fields.rpiCameraROI: Region of interest, in format x,y,width,height (all normalized between 0 and 1).
fields.rpiCameraHDR: Whether to enable HDR on Raspberry Camera 3.
fields.rpiCameraMode: Sensor mode, in format [width]:[height]:[bit-depth]:[packing]. Bit-depth and packing are optional.
fields.rpiCameraLensPosition: Lens position (for manual autofocus only), set to focus at a specific distance calculated by d = 1 / value. Examples: 0 → infinity; 0.5 → objects 2 m away; 2 → objects 50 cm away.
fields.rpiCameraAfWindow: Autofocus window, in the form x,y,width,height where the coordinates are given as a proportion of the entire image.
fields.rpiCameraFlickerPeriod: Manual flicker correction period, in microseconds.
fields.rpiCameraTextOverlayEnable: Enables printing text on each frame.
fields.rpiCameraTextOverlay: Text that is printed on each frame. Format is the one of the strftime() function.
fields.rpiCameraCodec: Codec (auto, hardwareH264, softwareH264 or mjpeg). When auto, it defaults to: hardwareH264 when stream is primary and hardware encoder is available; softwareH264 when stream is primary and hardware encoder is not available; mjpeg when stream is secondary.
fields.rpiCameraIDRPeriod: Period between IDR frames (when codec is hardwareH264 or softwareH264).
fields.rpiCameraBitrate: Bitrate (when codec is hardwareH264 or softwareH264).
fields.rpiCameraH264Profile: H264 profile (auto, baseline, main or high). When auto, it defaults to: main when codec is hardwareH264; baseline when codec is softwareH264.
fields.forward: Forward the stream of this path to one or more external servers.
fields.forwardDest: Forward destination. Can be rtsp://, rtsps://, rtmp://…#streamKey, rtmps://…#streamKey, srt://host:port?streamid=…, moqt://…, whip://host:port/path/whip, or whips://host:port/path/whip. Variables: $MTX_PATH (path name), $G1, $G2, … (regex groups if path name is a regex).
fields.forwardDestFingerprint: If the destination TLS certificate is self-signed or invalid, you can provide the fingerprint of the certificate in order to validate it anyway.
fields.forwardMoqTransport: Transport protocol used when forwarding with Media-over-QUIC. Available values are quic, webtransport.
fields.forwardWhipBearerToken: Token to insert in the Authorization: Bearer header when using WHIP.
fields.runOnInit: Command to run when this path is initialized. This can be used to publish a stream when the server is launched. This is terminated with SIGINT when the program closes.
fields.runOnInitRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnDemand: Command to run when this path is requested by a reader and no one is publishing to this path yet. This can be used to publish a stream on demand. This is terminated with SIGINT when there are no readers anymore.
fields.runOnDemandRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnDemandStartTimeout: Readers will be put on hold until the runOnDemand command starts publishing or until this amount of time has passed.
fields.runOnDemandCloseAfter: The command will be closed when there are no readers connected and this amount of time has passed.
fields.runOnUnDemand: Command to run when there are no readers anymore.
fields.runOnAvailable: Command to run when the stream is available to be read. This is terminated with SIGINT when the stream is not available anymore.
fields.runOnAvailableRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnUnavailable: Command to run when the stream is not available anymore.
fields.runOnOnline: Command to run when the stream is online, which means that the stream is available and provided by an online source (not an offline segment). This is terminated with SIGINT when the stream is not online anymore.
fields.runOnOnlineRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnOffline: Command to run when the stream is not online anymore.
fields.runOnRead: Command to run when a client starts reading. This is terminated with SIGINT when a client stops reading.
fields.runOnReadRestart: Restart the command if it exits.
fields.runOnUnread: Command to run when a client stops reading.
fields.runOnRecordSegmentCreate: Command to run when a recording segment is created.
fields.runOnRecordSegmentComplete: Command to run when a recording segment is complete.
fields.user: Username. any means any user, including anonymous ones.
fields.pass: Password. Not used in case of any user.
fields.ips: IPs or networks allowed to use this user. An empty list means any IP.
fields.permissionsAction: Available actions are: publish, read, playback, api, metrics, pprof.
fields.permissionsPath: Paths can be set to further restrict access to a specific path. An empty path means any path. Regular expressions can be used by using a tilde as prefix.
fields.serverPort: TCP port on which the mediamtx-ui API listens.
fields.verbose: Enables verbose logging output of the server.
fields.mediamtxBaseUrl: Base URL of the MediaMTX Control API (e.g. http://localhost:9997).
fields.mediamtxAuthToken: Auth token for the MediaMTX API. Empty = delete token.
fields.mediamtxApiVersion: Version of the MediaMTX Control API (e.g. v3).
fields.mediamtxBridgeTimeout: Timeout for bridge calls to MediaMTX in milliseconds.
fields.apiBaseUrl: Base path of the own API (default /v3).
fields.hlsBaseUrl: Base URL of the HLS playback server. Empty = current origin (window.location.origin).
fields.playbackBaseUrl: Base URL of the playback server. Empty = current origin + port from playbackAddress.
fields.theme: Color theme of the interface (dark or light).
fields.primaryHue: Hue of the primary color (0–360). Saturation and lightness stay fixed; replaces --color-primary.
fields.radiusFactor: Roundness factor (0–1). Scales all corner radii; replaces --radius-factor.
fields.autoRefreshMs: Interval in ms at which data is automatically reloaded. 0 = off.
fields.itemsPerPage: Number of entries displayed per page.

validation.mustBeOneOf: {{label}} must be one of the allowed options
